units.translation: especially of things touching the body, such as clothing, arms, or those carried in the hands, and in expressions which, like σὺν τάχει [with speed], σὺν τύχη [with fortune], σὺν δίκη [with justice], σὺν χρόνῳ [with time], have the force of adverbs.
σὺν τοῖσδε [with these] is wrongly read by Triclinius for καὶ τοῖσδε [and these].

Thus Porson for συμπνοαῖς [with breaths], i.e. σὺμ πνοαῖς [with breaths], which is the old orthography, often preserved in old manuscripts, as Sept. 487 ξύμβοῇ [with a shout] M at first hand, changed to ξύν [with] by a second hand. Further Sept. 661 σύμ φοίτῳ [with wandering] and συμβασιλεῦσι [with kings] 764. Suppl. 158 ἱξόμεσθα σὺν κλάδοις [we shall come with branches]. 187 ὠμῇ ξὺν ὀργῇ [with savage anger]. 610 κἀρρυσιάστους ξύν τ᾿ ἀσυλία βροτῶν [and unplundered, with inviolability from mortals]. 614 ἄτιμον εἶναι ξὺν φυγῇ δημηλάτω [to be dishonored with exile driven by the people]. 845 δεσποσίῳ ξὺν ὕβρει [with masterful insolence]. 975 ξύν τ᾽ εὐκλείᾳ καὶ ἀμηνίτῳ βάξει τάσσεσθε [and with good repute and unresentful report you are stationed]. 1072 ξὺν εὐχαῖς ἐμαῖς λυτηρίοις [with my prayers of deliverance].
